# How much does the annual fund drive raise?

Every fall Hubbard Hall mails an annual-fund appeal. Neon codes gifts to an
`Annual Fund Drive` campaign for each drive back to FY13, which allows two measures that
answer different questions and are worth keeping apart:

- **In the window** — gifts dated October 1 through January 31 of the drive's fiscal
  year, the four months after the letter mails: how the mailed appeal itself performed.
- **Total coded to the drive** — everything ever coded to that drive's campaign,
  whenever it arrived: what the drive ultimately brought in.

The fall 2025 drive's in-window giving is examined household-by-household in
[Who responded to the fall 2025 appeal?](10-appeal-response.html); this chapter steps
back to the year-by-year series. See [Methodology](99-methodology.html) for the
clean-gift basis (business gifts coded to a drive, about $21k across all years, are
excluded).

```{python}
#| label: setup-fund-drive
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from hh.viz import style, BLUE

from hh.clean.accounts import clean_accounts
from hh.clean.donations import clean_donations
from hh.analytics.campaigns import annual_drive_by_year

tab = annual_drive_by_year(clean_donations(accounts=clean_accounts()))
tab = tab.loc[tab.index <= pd.Timestamp.today().year]  # drop the drive not yet mailed
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-fund-drive
show = tab.copy()
show.index = [f"FY{y - 2000}" for y in show.index]
show.index.name = "Drive (fiscal year)"
show["gifts"] = show["gifts"].astype(int)
show["households"] = show["households"].astype(int)
for c in ("oct_jan", "later", "total", "median_window_gift", "top_window_gift"):
    show[c] = show[c].map("${:,.0f}".format)
show = show.rename(columns={"oct_jan": "in window (Oct–Jan)", "later": "later, still coded",
                            "total": "total coded", "median_window_gift": "median in-window gift",
                            "top_window_gift": "largest in-window gift"})
show
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-fund-drive
#| column: page
long = tab.reset_index().melt(id_vars="drive", value_vars=["oct_jan", "later"],
                              var_name="When", value_name="Dollars")
long["FY"] = long["drive"].map(lambda y: f"FY{y - 2000}")
long["When"] = long["When"].map({"oct_jan": "In window (Oct–Jan)",
                                 "later": "Later, still coded to the drive"})
fig = px.bar(long, x="FY", y="Dollars", color="When",
             color_discrete_sequence=[BLUE, "#b3cde3"])
style(fig).show()
```

What the series shows:

```{python}
#| label: fund-drive-notes
#| output: asis
#| echo: false
pre = tab.loc[tab.index <= 2019, "oct_jan"].mean()
post = tab.loc[tab.index >= 2020, "oct_jan"].mean()
d21 = tab.loc[2021]
print(f"- **The window measure is steadier and recently stronger.** In-window giving "
      f"averaged about ${pre:,.0f} across the fall 2012-2019 drives and ${post:,.0f} "
      f"across fall 2020-2025, on household counts that barely moved. The best window "
      f"on record is the fall 2020 pandemic drive (${d21['oct_jan']:,.0f} from "
      f"{int(d21['households'])} households, with a largest gift of only "
      f"${d21['top_window_gift']:,.0f}).")
print("- **The gap between the two measures is concentrated, not diffuse.** In most "
      "years a single recurring five-figure gift arrives just after the window closes, "
      "and mid-decade drives carry sizable later-coded tails (spring gifts carrying the "
      "campaign label), so total-coded exceeds the window by anywhere from under ten "
      "percent to a factor of three.")
print("- **The typical gift has not changed.** The median in-window gift sits between "
      "$70 and $100 in every drive on record.")
print("- A separate **Summer-Fall 2022 matching campaign** (about $28k, FY23) ran "
      "alongside that year's drive and is not included in these figures.")
```
